summary.headline: Sejal Glass Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.14% to INR139.86 crores, with EBITDA margin at 18.35% and PAT margin at 10.31%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 total income grew 33.14% YoY to INR139.86 crores, EBITDA rose 43.44% to INR25.66 crores, and net profit rose 77.61% to INR14.42 crores. Management attributed margin gains mainly to COGS improvement from product mix, raw material sourcing, and better utilisation at Erode and Taloja. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 25% to 40%, EBITDA margin of about 18% and PAT margin of about 10%. Specialty products (fire-rated, railway-grade, digital print) remain at a very small base, with fire-rated commercial sales targeted from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: India - Erode and Taloja (Glasstech, acquired April 2025)
segments.commentary: Erode EBITDA is about 10% positive; Taloja is around break-even. Tempering utilisation at Taloja rose to 69% from 55% QoQ, and IG to about 40% from 24%. Erode tempering rose to over 24% from 13%, and IG to over 18% from under 5%.

segments.name: UAE (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: IG capacity utilisation is about 90%, with a third tempering line due in Q3 FY27. Management said UAE COGS improved to 3% of sales, and the facade division contributed to EBITDA this quarter. Management expects UAE revenue of about INR350 crores in FY27.

segments.name: India - Silvassa
segments.commentary: IG utilisation was 43% in Q2 FY27, and management targets 50% by FY27 driven by project sales of IG and laminated glass.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25% to 40% YoY.
EBITDA margin expected at about 18% for FY27, with H2 at about 18%.
Fire-rated glass: trial run on the floor in Q3 FY27 and commercial sales from Q4 FY27; guidance on fire-rated revenue only in Q1 FY28.
Specialty products expected at about 5% of FY27 revenue and 15% to 20% in FY28.
Management expects peak revenue of about INR600 to INR650 crores from existing infrastructure, targeted for FY28.
Long-term India-UAE revenue mix target of 60:40 (UAE:India).
capex_capacity: Annual production capacity is about 61.94 lakh square meters across Silvassa, Taloja, Erode (India) and Ras Al Khaimah (UAE).
UAE tempering third line and fire-rated facilities require about AED20 million capex, funded 60% internal accruals and 40% bank finance.
Fire-rated glass line imported and being installed in India; trial production and approvals targeted by end Q3 FY27.
Peak utilisation target: above 85% for IG and laminates; tempering near 100% since it feeds IG and laminate.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions or capacity additions, with nothing concrete to disclose.
demand_pricing: Order book: UAE about AED78 million as of September 2026, for delivery over 6 to 9 months; India about INR80 to 85 crores (management gave both figures), delivered over 6 to 8 month project cycles.
July 2026 UAE orders of AED27.6 million (about INR71 crores) across five projects; domestic orders of about INR150 crores were also cited.
Railway: more than INR100 crores of tenders per quarter; bid-win ratio stated at under 5%. Company is an approved vendor at three railway coach factories.
Exports from India started about a year ago to Israel and Cyprus, with Sri Lanka added this year; Africa and Europe are under 5% of revenue.
Management cited an Indian glass industry of more than USD3.9 billion, with architectural/processed glass above 60%. Fire-rated market estimated above INR500 crores across India and UAE.
Management said Middle East logistics and shipping costs rose, but it passed input cost increases on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the improvement, and what growth, margin and cash flow do you expect for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain to COGS improvement from product mix and utilisation, and expects EBITDA of about 18% for FY27. It guided revenue growth of 25% to 40%.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation levels and margins at Taloja and Erode?
qa_highlights.answer: Erode is about 10% EBITDA positive and Taloja is near break-even. Utilisation has improved QoQ, with Taloja tempering at 69% and Erode tempering at 24%+.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit grow more slowly than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation at Erode and Taloja, UAE COGS down to 3%, manpower and machine efficiency, and the UAE facade division.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak utilisation target and what is the fire-rated opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak target is above 85% for IG and laminates, with tempering near 100%. Fire-rated EBITDA margin is expected above 30%, and guidance will come in Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term bank debt is repaid through regular EMIs, with no prepayment or debt reduction plan at present.

qa_highlights.question: Is geopolitical tension in the Middle East affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business is doing well despite tensions. Logistics and shipping costs rose, and these were passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: In the UAE, about 25% of business is under LC, with the rest on PDCs. In India, buying specified coated glass in advance ties up working capital, and profits are being ploughed back into working capital.

risks_watch: Specialty products (fire-rated, railway, digital print) remain very small, and their FY27 5% and FY28 15% to 20% contribution targets depend on commercial launches.
Railway bid-win ratio is under 5%, and the company is still at vendor category C.
Taloja is only at break-even, so India margin depends on utilisation ramp.
Middle East geopolitics and rising freight costs.
Working capital remains a drag: India project inventory is pre-purchased and cash flow is described as weak.
Management gave two different India order book figures (INR80 crores and INR85 crores) during the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and growth, with specific utilisation numbers. Less precise on specialty product timelines and on working capital, where answers were more general. The call had some transcription gaps and a line drop during Q&A.
key_quotes: No, we are at 18% plus right now in quarter two, and we are expecting to be more or less about 18% in the second half also.
Margins will be definitely more in terms of EBITDA, it is more than 30%, because it is a very value-added product.
So, the tempering third line and the fire-rated and the other facilities to be required to make this operation is around in the range of AED20 million of our total investment in terms of capex.
